Combined Efficiency (All 3 pipes) = 588 ÷ 42 = 14 units/min.

Time to empty = 588 ÷ 13 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 588/13 min.**

questions.question: The equivalent fraction of 2.777... is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The repeating decimal is: 2.777...

**Formula used:**

Let x = 2.777... (a repeating decimal)

Multiply both sides by 10ⁿ (where n is the number of repeating digits) to eliminate the repeating part.

Then solve for x.

**Calculations:**

Let x = 2.777...

Multiply by 10 (since 1 digit is repeating):

⇒ 10x = 27.777...

Now subtract the original equation (x = 2.777...) from this:

⇒ 10x - x = 27.777... - 2.777...

⇒ 9x = 25

⇒ x = 25/9

**∴ The equivalent fraction of 2.777... is (25/9), and the correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Standard base pairing in DNA occurs due to which type of bonding?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hydrogen bonding**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **DNA**, the two complementary strands are held together by **hydrogen bonds** between the nitrogenous bases.
 
• **Adenine (A)** always pairs with **Thymine (T)** through two hydrogen bonds, while **Guanine (G)** pairs with **Cytosine (C)** using three hydrogen bonds.
 
• This specific pairing is known as **complementary base pairing**, which is essential for the accurate replication of genetic material.
 
• **Hydrogen bonds** are weak, non-covalent interactions that allow the double helix structure of DNA to unzip during replication and transcription.
 
• Although individually weak, the cumulative effect of a large number of hydrogen bonds provides structural **stability** to the DNA double helix.
 
• The double helix model of DNA was first proposed by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick**, and their discovery highlighted the role of hydrogen bonding in maintaining DNA’s structural integrity.
 
• These bonds ensure that mutations are minimized by enabling **specificity** in base pairing during DNA replication.
 
• Hydrogen bonding occurs due to the difference in **electronegativity** between the hydrogen atom and the electronegative atoms (e.g., oxygen or nitrogen) involved in the base pairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ionic bonding**__

 __
 
• **Ionic bonds** occur due to the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, which is not relevant in the context of DNA base pairing.
 
• Examples of ionic bonding are typically found in compounds like **sodium chloride (NaCl)**.
 
• In DNA, ionic interactions are involved in the stabilization of the double helix through interactions between the negatively charged **phosphate backbone** and positively charged ions, but they are not responsible for base pairing.
 
 
 
• **Van Der Waals interactions**__
 __
 
• **Van Der Waals forces** are weak, short-range forces that arise from fluctuating dipoles, contributing to DNA’s overall structural stability.
 
• These interactions are present between stacked bases in the DNA double helix, known as **base stacking interactions**, but they do not play a direct role in base pairing.
 
 
 
• **Covalent bonding**__
 
 
• **Covalent bonds** involve the sharing of electron pairs between atoms, and they are responsible for the formation of the **sugar-phosphate backbone** in DNA.
 
• These bonds are much stronger than hydrogen bonds and provide the primary structure of DNA, but they do not mediate base pairing.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas** are not part of the outer boundary of the **Peninsular Plateau**. The Peninsular Plateau is primarily confined to the southern part of India, while the Himalayas are located in the northern region.
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is a massive landmass that includes the **Deccan Plateau**, **Malwa Plateau**, and the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**.
 
• The **Himalayas** are young fold mountains formed due to the collision of the **Indian Plate** with the **Eurasian Plate**. They are geologically distinct from the Peninsular Plateau, which is considered one of the oldest landforms of India.
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is characterized by its stable geological structure, being part of the **Indian Shield**, whereas the Himalayas are tectonically active.
 
• The Himalayas act as a natural barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the rest of Asia. They are known for their high peaks, including **Mount Everest**, which is the highest peak in the world.
 
• Unlike the Peninsular Plateau, which is surrounded by rivers like the **Godavari** and **Krishna**, the Himalayas give rise to major perennial rivers such as the **Ganges**, **Brahmaputra**, and **Indus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• These hills are part of the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**, which is a constituent of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The region is known for its rich **basaltic rocks**, formed due to volcanic activity during the **Cretaceous period.**
 
 
 
• **Delhi Ridge**__
 __
 
• The **Delhi Ridge** is the northernmost extension of the **Aravalli Range**.
 
• It is an integral part of the Peninsular Plateau and acts as a green lung for the city of Delhi.
 
• The ridge is significant for its **ecological importance**, helping maintain biodiversity and offering a natural barrier against desertification.
 
 
 
• **Gir Range**__
 
 
• The **Gir Range** is located in the state of **Gujarat**, forming part of the western region of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It is home to the **Gir National Park**, which is the only habitat of the **Asiatic lions**.
 
• Geologically, it is composed of ancient rocks and is surrounded by the **Saurashtra Plateau.**

questions.question: Which body primarily exercises the powers delegated through Article 243W of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Municipal Corporations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 243W of the Indian Constitution provides for the **functional responsibilities and powers** of **Municipalities**, which include **Municipal Corporations**, **Municipal Councils**, and **Nagar Panchayats**.
 
• The article is part of the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**, which introduced the concept of urban local governance in India.
 
• The functions under Article 243W include the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, implementation of schemes, and responsibilities related to **urban infrastructure and services**, such as water supply, sanitation, and urban planning.
 
• **Municipal Corporations** are established in larger cities and are responsible for urban development, governance, and providing essential services such as **roads, education, health care, waste management, and street lighting.**
 
• The powers and responsibilities delegated to Municipal Corporations are outlined in the **12th Schedule** of the Constitution, which includes **18 functional areas**, such as urban planning, regulation of land use, slum improvement, public health, and more.
 
• The **State Legislature** is responsible for defining the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities under Article 243W.
 
• Municipal Corporations ensure the implementation of policies and schemes at the urban level, contributing to **decentralized governance** as envisaged by the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parliament of India**__

 __
 
• The **Parliament of India** is the supreme legislative body in the country and consists of the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• Its role is to enact laws and policies, including constitutional amendments such as the **73rd and 74th Amendments**, which introduced Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies.
 
• While the Parliament provides a framework for governance, it does not directly exercise powers under Article 243W; these are delegated to urban local bodies like Municipal Corporations.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions**__
 __
 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** are responsible for rural governance and exercise powers under **Article 243G**, not Article 243W.
 
• PRIs operate at three levels: **Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti,** and **Zila Parishad**, focusing on rural development and decentralized governance.
 
• They handle functions related to **agriculture, rural infrastructure, and poverty alleviation**, as outlined in the **11th Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**__
 
 
• The **State Legislature** plays a critical role in defining the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipal Corporations and other urban local bodies under Article 243W.
 
• It establishes laws and frameworks for governance at the urban level, including the enactment of state-specific **Municipal Acts**.
 
• However, it does not directly exercise the powers delegated under Article 243W; it delegates these to the urban local bodies.

questions.question: {If } sin A = (3)/(4), { then calculate } (2 cos A)/(sqrt{7)}.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin A = 3/4** (Perpendicular/Hypotenuse).

Using **Pythagorean triplet** logic: **Base = √(4² − 3²) = √(16 − 9) = √7**.

Then **cos A = Base/Hypotenuse = √7/4**.

Value required = (2 × √7/4) ÷ √7 = 2/4 = 1/2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ea5125cabf7aea45365439f865943f206b5baf4b44648dcfbcdf0a5a25fe419.png] 

**Given:** sin A = 3/4

**Formula Used:** cos²A = 1 − sin²A

⇒ cos²A = 1 − (3/4)²

⇒ cos²A = 1 − 9/16 = 7/16

⇒ cos A = √7/4

⇒ Target Expression = (2 × cos A) / √7

⇒ Target Expression = (2 × (√7 / 4)) / √7

⇒ Target Expression = (2√7) / (4√7)

⇒ Target Expression = 2/4 = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For any angle A, sin A = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos A = Base/Hypotenuse, and tan A = Perpendicular/Base.

Pythagorean Identity

The fundamental identity is sin²A + cos²A = 1. This allows finding one ratio if the other is known.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².</p

questions.question: What will the amount after 1 year be, if ₹2,400 is invested at 20% compound interest per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes **half** (20% ÷ 2 = 10%) and time becomes **double** (1 year × 2 = 2 periods).

**Effective Rate** for 2 periods at 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = **21%**.

**Amount** = Principal × (100 + Effective Rate)% = 2400 × 121%

Amount = 24 × 121 = 2904

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,904.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹2,400**

Annual Rate (R) = **20%**

Time (T) = **1 year**

Compounding: **Half-yearly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e04704912691810094cd5be26028b5accf93d1492257694d3460072783720aed.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where r = **Half-yearly rate** and n = **Number of half-years**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ r = R ÷ 2 = 20% ÷ 2 = **10%**

⇒ n = T × 2 = 1 × 2 = **2 half-years**

⇒ A = 2400(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 2400(11/10)²

⇒ A = 2400 × (121/100)

⇒ A = 24 × 121

⇒ A = 2904

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,904.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compounding Half-Yearly

When interest is compounded semi-annually, the **nominal annual rate** is divided by 2, and the **number of years** is multiplied by 2.

Effective Annual Rate (EAR)

The actual interest earned in a year. Formula: EAR = (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where n is the number of compounding periods per year.

CI vs SI Difference for 2 Periods

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for two periods is given by P(r/100)².

After 7 months, Y withdrew his 33% share, while Z withdrew his 24% share 5 months prior to the completion of the year. If the total profit at the end of year is ₹16,100, find the share of Z (in ₹) in the profit.

Ratio of **Profit** is based on **Investment × Time**.

Ratio of Investment X : Y : Z = 13 : 20 : 15.

X's share = 13 × 12 = 156.

Y's share = (20 × 7) + (20 × 0.67 × 5) = 140 + 67 = 207.

Z's share = (15 × 7) + (15 × 0.76 × 5) = 105 + 57 = 162.

Ratio X : Y : Z = 156 : 207 : 162 = 52 : 69 : 54.

Total units = 52 + 69 + 54 = 175. Share of Z = (54 ÷ 175) × 16100 = 54 × 92 = 4968.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,968.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ **X's Profit units** = 13 × 12 = 156 units.
⇒ **Y's Profit units**: Y withdrew 33% of 20 = 6.6. Remaining = 20 − 6.6 = 13.4.
⇒ Y = (20 × 7) + (13.4 × 5) = 140 + 67 = 207 units.

questions.question: Which of the following best encapsulates the fundamental difference between the von Neumann and Harvard architectures in computer systems?

options.text: The Harvard architecture allows simultaneous fetching of instructions and data, potentially improving performance, while the von Neumann architecture typically fetches them sequentially from the same memory space.
The von Neumann architecture utilises separate address spaces for instructions and data, while the Harvard architecture uses a single address space.

__
 
• The **von Neumann architecture** uses a single memory space for both **instructions** and **data**, meaning the CPU fetches them sequentially. This can lead to a bottleneck known as the **von Neumann bottleneck**, where the CPU waits for instructions or data due to limited bandwidth.
 
• In contrast, the **Harvard architecture** separates memory for instructions and data, allowing them to be accessed **simultaneously**. This separation can significantly improve performance, especially in systems requiring high-speed processing.
 
• The Harvard architecture is particularly useful in **embedded systems** and **real-time applications**, where deterministic performance is critical.
 
• The von Neumann architecture is widely used in **general-purpose computers**, as it simplifies the design and programming model by using a single memory space.
 
• The separation of memory in the Harvard architecture often requires more complex hardware, but it provides better **throughput** for specific tasks.
 
• Both architectures are foundational to modern computing, with hybrid systems often combining features of both to balance simplicity and performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** The von Neumann Architecture**__

 __
 
• Proposed by **John von Neumann** in the 1940s, this architecture forms the basis of most modern computers.
 
• It uses a single memory space where both **program instructions** and **data** are stored.
 
• The single memory architecture leads to what is called the **von Neumann bottleneck**, where the CPU waits for data or instructions due to limited memory bandwidth.
 
• Examples of devices using von Neumann architecture include **desktop computers**, **laptops**, and other general-purpose systems.
 
 
 
• ** The Harvard Architecture**__
 __
 
• This architecture was first used in the **Harvard Mark I** computer.
 
• It has **separate memory spaces** for instructions and data, allowing parallel access and higher performance.
 
• Commonly found in **microcontrollers** and **digital signal processors (DSPs)**.
 
• Examples of devices using Harvard architecture include **embedded systems**, such as those in automotive applications or industrial control systems.
 
 
 
• ** Hybrid Architectures**__
 
 
• Many modern processors combine features of both architectures to leverage the benefits of each.
 
• For instance, they may use a Harvard-like architecture internally for instruction and data caches while maintaining a von Neumann-like unified main memory.
 
• This hybrid approach is common in **modern CPUs** and **GPUs**.

questions.question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 14 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?

Let the **son's age 3 years ago** be **x**.

**Father's age 3 years ago** = 2x + 14.

Difference between their ages = (2x + 14) − x = **x + 14**.

The **age difference** remains constant; when the father is twice the son's age, the son's age must equal the difference (x + 14).

Future age of son = x + 14. Present age of son = x + 3.

Years from now = (x + 14) − (x + 3) = 11 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

⇒ F − 2S = 11 ...........(i)

⇒ (F + n) = 2(S + n)

⇒ F + n = 2S + 2n

⇒ n = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a key reason for judicial review in India?

options.text: To allow the judiciary to make laws
To maintain federal balance between Centre and States
To ensure the supremacy of the Parliament
To protect the supremacy of the Constitution and fundamental rights

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To protect the supremacy of the Constitution and fundamental rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial review** in India ensures the protection of the **supremacy of the Constitution**, which is the highest law of the land.
 
• It is a mechanism for safeguarding **fundamental rights**, as guaranteed under **Part III of the Indian Constitution**, against legislative and executive actions.
 
• The judiciary has the authority to review the actions and decisions of the legislature and executive to ensure they do not violate the **Constitutional provisions**.
 
• Judicial review enables the courts to declare laws or actions null and void if they are inconsistent with the Constitution.
 
• It upholds the principle of **constitutional morality**, ensuring that all laws and policies align with the values and principles enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• This process helps maintain the balance between the various organs of the government, preventing any one organ from exceeding its powers.
 
• Judicial review is crucial in a democracy like India, where the judiciary acts as the **guardian of the Constitution** and the rights of citizens.
 
• The concept finds its roots in **Articles 13, 32, and 226** of the Indian Constitution, which empower the judiciary to review laws and protect fundamental rights.
 
• It is especially significant in cases involving the violation of rights such as **freedom of speech**, **equality**, and **personal liberty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** To allow the judiciary to make laws**__

 __
 
• The judiciary does not have the power to **legislate**; its role is limited to interpreting and applying the law as per the Constitution.
 
• Law-making is the exclusive domain of the **legislature** in India, as per the separation of powers principle.
 
• Judicial review does not involve creating laws but reviewing them for **Constitutional validity**.
 
 
 
• **To maintain federal balance between Centre and States**__
 __
 
• While judicial review does play a role in resolving disputes between the **Centre and States**, this is not its primary purpose.
 
• Federal balance is maintained through mechanisms like the **Finance Commission** and specific provisions in the Constitution, such as **Article 246**, detailing the division of legislative powers.
 
 
 
• **To ensure the supremacy of the Parliament**__
 
 
• In India, the **Constitution**, not the Parliament, is supreme, unlike in the UK where parliamentary sovereignty exists.
 
• The judiciary reviews parliamentary laws to ensure they align with the **Constitutional framework**.
 
• Judicial review acts as a check on parliamentary supremacy, ensuring that laws do not violate **fundamental rights**.

questions.question: Which principle of citizenship did India start following more strictly after the 2003 Amendment?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Jus sanguinis (by blood)**__.

__
 
• After the **2003 Amendment** to the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, India shifted from the principle of **jus soli (citizenship by birth)** to a stricter application of **jus sanguinis (citizenship by descent).**
 
• The amendment introduced stricter conditions for acquiring Indian citizenship, especially for children born in India to foreign nationals.
 
• The focus was shifted to emphasize **ancestral ties**, meaning citizenship was granted based on the nationality of the parents rather than the place of birth.
 
• Under the revised law, a person born in India after **December 3, 2004**, can only claim Indian citizenship if at least one parent is an Indian citizen and the other parent is not an illegal migrant.
 
• The amendment aimed to address concerns over **illegal immigration** and its impact on demography and national security, especially in border states.
 
• The principle of **jus sanguinis** aligns with the concept of maintaining a closer connection to the nation through family lineage.
 
• This change brought India's citizenship laws more in line with countries that prioritize **descent-based citizenship**, such as Germany and Japan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jus soli (by birth)**__

 __
 
• The principle of **jus soli** grants citizenship to anyone born within a country's territory, regardless of their parents' nationality.
 
• Prior to the 2003 Amendment, India followed this principle for granting citizenship. For example, anyone born in India between **1950** and **1987** was automatically considered an Indian citizen.
 
• However, concerns over **illegal immigration** led to restrictions on this principle starting from **1987**, and it was further curtailed in the **2003 Amendment**.
 
• Countries like the **United States** still follow the principle of jus soli, granting automatic citizenship to anyone born on their soil.
 
 
 
• **Dual citizenship**__
 __
 
• India does not allow **dual citizenship**. The **Citizenship Act, 1955** mandates that Indian citizens must renounce their citizenship if they acquire the citizenship of another country.
 
• However, India allows individuals of Indian origin living abroad to obtain an **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card**, which provides certain privileges without granting full citizenship.
 
• Dual citizenship is practiced in some countries like **Canada** and the **United Kingdom**, allowing individuals to hold citizenship in more than one country simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Universal citizenship**__
 
 
• The concept of **universal citizenship** refers to the idea that all individuals belong to a global community and should have equal rights and opportunities regardless of their country of origin.
 
• This concept is more philosophical and is not implemented by any country in its legal framework.
 
• It contrasts with the traditional notions of citizenship, which are tied to national borders and sovereignty.

Net filling efficiency per minute = (1/8 − 1/11) = 3/88 of the tank.

Time to fill full tank = 88/3 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling pipe time = 8 min, Emptying pipe time = 11 min.

 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Inlet Pipe (+) 8 88 units +11 
 Outlet Pipe (−) 11 −8 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 11 − 8 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Required work = 3/4 of Total Capacity = 3/4 × 88 = 66 units.

⇒ Time required = Required work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 66 ÷ 3 = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Inlet pipes that fill the tank are taken as positive efficiency, while outlet pipes that empty the tank are taken as negative efficiency.

Net Time Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (y > x), net time to fill the tank = (xy) ÷ (y − x).

Work and Time Relationship

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. For a constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken.</p

questions.question: The mean and the mode of a data set are 51.5 and 61.7, respectively. Find the median of the data set, using the empirical formula.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **3 × Median = Mode + 2 × Mean**.

3 × Median = 61.7 + 2 × 51.5

3 × Median = 61.7 + 103 = 164.7

Median = 164.7 ÷ 3 = 54.9

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mean** = 51.5, **Mode** = 61.7

**Formula Used:** **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c43dd7a92943be8bd4363b53e8b8ed4ad7088dd48727cde72641a27b5229c3c1.png] 

⇒ 61.7 = 3 × Median − 2 × 51.5

⇒ 61.7 = 3 × Median − 103

⇒ 3 × Median = 61.7 + 103

⇒ 3 × Median = 164.7

⇒ Median = 164.7 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 54.9

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the relationship between central tendencies is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical.

Skewness and Central Tendency

In **positively skewed** data, Mean > Median > Mode. In **negatively skewed** data, Mode > Median > Mean.</p

questions.question: The downstream speed is 22 km/hr and the upstream speed is 5.5 km/hr. It takes a boat a total of 8 hours to go to a place and come back. What is the total distance travelled by the boat?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Downstream Speed** to **Upstream Speed** = 22 : 5.5 = 4 : 1.

Since **Distance** is constant for one way, **Time ratio** = Inverse of speed ratio = 1 : 4.

Total time units = 1 + 4 = 5 units → 8 hours. So, 1 unit = 8/5 hours.

One-way distance = Speed × Time = 22 × (8/5) = 176/5 km.

**Total distance** (Round trip) = 2 × (176/5) = 352/5 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 352/5 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a443fb0831564c76ef48fbd84cfe51f9a45afb67b3830ffaca877942305f2fff.png] 

**Given:**

**Downstream speed (D)** = 22 km/hr

**Upstream speed (U)** = 5.5 km/hr

**Total time (T)** = 8 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = (Distance / Downstream Speed) + (Distance / Upstream Speed)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the one-way distance be **d**.

⇒ (d / 22) + (d / 5.5) = 8

⇒ (d / 22) + (2d / 11) = 8

⇒ (d + 4d) / 22 = 8

⇒ 5d / 22 = 8

⇒ 5d = 176

⇒ d = 176/5 km

⇒ **Total distance travelled** = 2 × d = 2 × (176/5) = 352/5 km

**∴ The correct answer is 352/5 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water and Current

Speed of boat in **still water** (u) = (D + U) / 2 and speed of **current** (v) = (D − U) / 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average speed for the entire journey = (2 × D × U) / (D + U). Total Distance = Average Speed × Total Time.

Relative Speed Concept

Downstream speed includes the **velocity of the stream** helping the boat, whereas upstream speed is against the stream.</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **third number** is 100.

First number = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130.

Second number = 100 + 18% of 100 = 118.

Ratio = 130 : 118 = 65 : 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 65 : 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number is 30% more than the third. Second number is 18% more than the third.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf5890a9fcc82bd47a830645f69776bd44acc133a43d06caaee58c1d942fddd5.png] 

Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ First number = x + 0.30x = 1.30x

⇒ Second number = x + 0.18x = 1.18x

⇒ Ratio = First number ÷ Second number

⇒ Ratio = 1.30x ÷ 1.18x

⇒ Ratio = 130 / 118

⇒ Ratio = 65 / 59

**∴ The correct answer is 65 : 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

In percentage problems comparing multiple items to one common item, assume the common item (base) as 100 for easier calculation.</p

questions.question: If x + (1)/(x) = 4 , then the value of x³ + (1)/(x³) is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **x + 1/x = k**, then **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Given: **x + 1/x = 4** ⇒ **k = 4**.

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 4³ − 3 × 4

⇒ 64 − 12 = 52.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: **x + 1/x = 4**

Formula Used: **(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)**

Let **a = x** and **b = 1/x**.

⇒ (x + 1/x)³ = x³ + (1/x)³ + 3 × x × (1/x) × (x + 1/x)

⇒ (4)³ = x³ + 1/x³ + 3 × (x + 1/x)

⇒ 64 = x³ + 1/x³ + 3 × 4

⇒ 64 = x³ + 1/x³ + 12

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 64 − 12

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 52

Therefore, the value is 52, which corresponds to **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square of a Sum Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. This is derived from (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2.

Cube of a Difference Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k. This is derived from (x − 1/x)³ = x³ − 1/x³ − 3(x − 1/x).

Fourth Power Identity

To find x⁴ + 1/x⁴, square the result of x² + 1/x² and subtract 2: x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2.</p

questions.question: What type of shrine is the Neeramankara Temple located in Nemam, Kerala, in India known to be?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sandhara type**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neeramankara Temple**, located in **Nemam, Kerala**, is known to be built in the **Sandhara type** of shrine architecture.
 
• The term **Sandhara** refers to a type of temple layout in which the structure is **enclosed by walls** and has a **circumambulatory path** (pradakshina patha) around the sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• Such temples are designed to allow devotees to perform **pradakshina (circumambulation)** of the deity housed in the sanctum.
 
• This architectural style is commonly found in **Indian temple architecture**, particularly in regions where cultural and religious practices emphasize circumambulation as an integral part of worship.
 
• The **Neeramankara Temple** reflects the traditional **Kerala temple architecture**, with its unique wooden carvings, sloped roofs, and intricate design elements.
 
• The temple is a significant **spiritual and cultural center** in the region, drawing devotees and architecture enthusiasts alike.
 
• Sandhara temples often include additional features such as **mandapas (pillared halls)** and **ornamental gateways**, enhancing the aesthetic and functional aspects of the shrine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sarvatobhadra type**__

 __
 
• The **Sarvatobhadra** type of temple architecture is characterized by its **symmetry and accessibility from all directions**.
 
• This type of temple often has entrances on all four sides, symbolizing the universal accessibility of the deity housed within.
 
• It is commonly found in **North Indian temple architecture**.
 
• Unlike the Sandhara type, it may or may not have a circumambulatory path.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa type**__
 __
 
• A **Mandapa** is a **pillared hall** or pavilion used for religious purposes, particularly in Hindu temples.
 
• It is typically situated in front of the sanctum and serves as a place for **devotees to gather** and participate in rituals.
 
• While Mandapas are part of temple complexes, they are not a standalone architectural style like Sandhara or Sarvatobhadra.
 
 
 
• **Nirandhara type**__
 
 
• The **Nirandhara** type of temple is characterized by the **absence of a circumambulatory path** around the sanctum.
 
• It focuses solely on the central sanctum and does not include space for devotees to perform pradakshina.
 
• These temples are typically smaller and emphasize **direct worship** of the deity without circumambulation.

questions.question: If the ratio of two numbers is 18 : 5 and the product of their LCM and their HCF is 360, then the sum of the reciprocals of the LCM and the HCF is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let HCF = x. Since the ratio of the numbers is 18 : 5, their LCM = 18 × 5 × x = 90x.

Product of LCM and HCF = 90x × x = 90x² = 360 ⇒ x² = 4 ⇒ x = 2.

So, HCF = 2 and LCM = 180.

Sum of their reciprocals = (1 / 180) + (1 / 2) = (1 + 90) / 180 = 91 / 180.

**∴ The correct answer is 91/180.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers = 18 : 5

Product of their LCM and HCF = 360

**Formula Used:**

For two numbers in ratio a : b (where a and b are coprime) with HCF = x, LCM = a × b × x.

 
 Ratio = 18 : 5
 
 Numbers: 18x and 5x
 

 

 
 HCF = x
 
 LCM = 18 × 5 × x = 90x
 LCM × HCF = 90x² = 360

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 18x and 5x.

⇒ Since 18 and 5 are coprime to each other, their highest common factor (HCF) is x.

⇒ The least common multiple (LCM) of 18x and 5x = 18 × 5 × x = 90x.

⇒ Given, product of LCM and HCF = 360.

⇒ 90x × x = 360

⇒ 90x² = 360

⇒ x² = 360 ÷ 90 = 4

⇒ x = √4 = 2

⇒ Therefore, HCF = 2 and LCM = 90 × 2 = 180.

⇒ Sum of reciprocals of LCM and HCF = (1 / LCM) + (1 / HCF)

⇒ Sum of reciprocals = (1 / 180) + (1 / 2)

⇒ Sum of reciprocals = (1 + 90) / 180 = 91 / 180.

**∴ The correct answer is 91/180.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between HCF, LCM and Product of Numbers

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: A × B = HCF × LCM.

Numbers from Ratio

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b, then the numbers can be represented as (a × HCF) and (b × HCF). Here, a and b are strictly co-prime terms.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). Similarly, LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).
</p

questions.question: Which revolution in India is associated with the growth of the fishing industry?

__
 
• The **Blue Revolution** is associated with the **growth of the fishing industry** in India.
 
• It refers to the significant increase in the production of **fish and marine products** through advanced techniques such as **aquaculture** and better management practices.
 
• The revolution aimed to improve **aquatic resources** and ensure better utilization of water bodies for fish farming.
 
• The **Fish Farmers Development Agency (FFDA)** and **National Fisheries Development Board** were key organizations that supported the initiatives under the Blue Revolution.
 
• The Blue Revolution also focused on enhancing **employment opportunities** in the fisheries sector, benefitting rural and coastal communities.
 
• India became one of the world's largest producers of fish due to the initiatives under this revolution, contributing significantly to its **food security** and **export earnings**.
 
• The Blue Revolution is crucial for ensuring sustainable management of aquatic ecosystems while meeting the growing demand for **fish and seafood**.
 
• It also included the development of **marine fisheries**, **inland fisheries**, and **brackish water aquaculture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **White Revolution**__

 __
 
• The **White Revolution** in India is associated with the **production and growth of milk**.
 
• This revolution was spearheaded by **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, known as the father of the White Revolution.
 
• It led to India becoming the largest producer of milk in the world and promoted **self-sufficiency in dairy production**.
 
• The initiative was implemented through the **Operation Flood** program launched by the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)**.
 
• The White Revolution contributed significantly to improving **nutrition levels**, enhancing **livelihoods**, and reducing dependency on imports.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**__
 __
 
• The **Green Revolution** refers to the significant increase in **agricultural production** in India during the 1960s and 1970s.
 
• It focused on the use of **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds**, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation techniques.
 
• It transformed India into a nation self-sufficient in food grains, especially **wheat and rice**.
 
• This revolution was led by **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan**, known as the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• The Green Revolution also had a major impact on reducing **famine risks** and improving **food security**.
 
 
 
• **Yellow Revolution**__
 
 
• The **Yellow Revolution** in India is associated with the **production and growth of edible oil**, particularly **mustard and sunflower oil**.
 
• It aimed to reduce India's dependence on imported edible oils and achieve **self-reliance** in oilseed production.
 
• The revolution focused on improving **oilseed cultivation techniques** and promoting the use of **hybrid varieties**.
 
• The Yellow Revolution also supported rural livelihoods by enhancing **oilseed farming** opportunities.

questions.question: Anil bought the first pen for ₹100 and the second pen for ₹160, respectively. He sells the first pen at 15% of the profit but the buyer bargains for the price, and he has to offer a 29% discount and the second pen at 58% of the profit. Find the total profit he had in this transaction (correct to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **Pen 1**: MP = 100 × 1.15 = 115. SP = 115 × (1 − 0.29) = 115 × 0.71 = 81.65.

Profit/Loss 1 = 81.65 − 100 = **−18.35**.

For **Pen 2**: Profit 2 = 160 × 58% = 160 × 0.58 = **92.80**.

Total Profit = 92.80 − 18.35 = **74.45**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹74.45.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: CP₁ = ₹100, Profit% applied for MP = 15%, Discount = 29%, CP₂ = ₹160, Profit%₂ = 58%.

Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100 | Final SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100 | Profit = Total SP − Total CP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d2d1d23eb8239968c993f380eb9cd4b926418adfa3ff8534dc09283d24a63ec.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Calculate marked price for the first pen. MP₁ = 100 + (15% of 100) = ₹115.

⇒ **Step 2:** Calculate selling price for the first pen after discount. SP₁ = 115 − (29% of 115) = 115 − 33.35 = ₹81.65.

⇒ **Step 3:** Calculate selling price for the second pen. SP₂ = 160 + (58% of 160) = 160 + 92.8 = ₹252.8.

⇒ **Step 4:** Calculate total Cost Price and total Selling Price. Total CP = 100 + 160 = ₹260. Total SP = 81.65 + 252.8 = ₹334.45.

⇒ **Step 5:** Calculate total Profit. Profit = 334.45 − 260 = ₹74.45.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹74.45.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Marked Price is the price listed by the seller. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** to arrive at the Selling Price: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.

Profit Calculation

Profit is the difference between the **Selling Price** and the **Cost Price**. If SP is less than CP, it results in a loss.

questions.question: Effective Revenue Deficit was introduced in the government budgeting during which year?

__
 
• **Effective Revenue Deficit** was introduced in **2011-12** during the **Union Budget of India**.
 
• The concept was introduced to distinguish between revenue expenditure that creates assets and other types of revenue expenditure.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting the **Grants for Creation of Capital Assets** from the Revenue Deficit.
 
• This measure was introduced to give a clearer picture of the actual deficit that impacts the fiscal position of the government.
 
• The **primary goal** of Effective Revenue Deficit is to promote transparency in public finance and encourage capital asset creation.
 
• It helps in understanding how much of the revenue expenditure is contributing to the creation of assets, which is a long-term benefit for the economy.
 
• This concept aligns with the government's efforts to improve fiscal discipline and ensure efficient allocation of resources.
 
• It is significant for policymakers and economists as it provides insights into the government's financial health and investment in infrastructure and development projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** 2003-04**__

 __
 
• The year **2003** is significant in Indian fiscal policy due to the introduction of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act**.
 
• The FRBM Act aims to ensure responsible fiscal management and reduce fiscal deficits.
 
• It laid down targets for reducing the **Revenue Deficit** and **Fiscal Deficit**, but it did not include the concept of Effective Revenue Deficit.
 
 
 
• **2015-16**__
 __
 
• The year **2015-16** is associated with several fiscal reforms, but the concept of Effective Revenue Deficit was already introduced prior to this period.
 
• During this time, the government focused on fiscal consolidation and initiatives like **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states about the directive for states to make provision for public assistance in cases of unemployment?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 41**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 41** of the Constitution of India is a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• It directs the state to make effective provisions for **securing the right to work, education, and public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and other cases of undeserved want.
 
• The provision under Article 41 is **non-justiciable**, meaning it cannot be enforced by courts, but it acts as a guiding principle for the state while formulating policies.
 
• Article 41 emphasizes the responsibility of the state to consider its **economic capacity and development** while implementing these provisions.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** aim to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order informed by justice—social, economic, and political.
 
• Article 41 is particularly relevant in addressing **social and economic inequalities**, ensuring that vulnerable sections of society receive adequate support.
 
• The article complements other provisions like **Article 39**, which focus on equitable distribution of resources, and **Article 42**, which deals with just and humane conditions of work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Article 39**__

 __
 
• **Article 39** is also a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It mandates the state to ensure that the **ownership and control of material resources** of the community are distributed to serve the common good.
 
• It also emphasizes preventing the concentration of wealth and means of production to the detriment of the common interest.
 
• Additionally, Article 39 focuses on providing children with opportunities to develop in a healthy manner and protecting them against exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Article 42**__
 __
 
• **Article 42** directs the state to make provisions for securing **just and humane conditions of work** and for maternity relief.
 
• This article aims to improve the quality of labor conditions and is particularly significant for the welfare of women and workers.
 
• It complements labor laws and policies, ensuring social justice for working individuals.
 
 
 
• **Article 40**__
 
 
• **Article 40** deals with the organization of **village panchayats**.
 
• It directs the state to take steps to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as **units of self-government**.
 
• This article is crucial for strengthening **grassroots democracy** in India.

questions.question: A cube of side 10 cm is cut into cubes of side 2 cm. Calculate the total surface area (in cm²) of all the small cubes:

questions.question: The average of three numbers is 23. If two of them are 11 and 26, the third number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total of **three numbers** = Average × 3 = 23 × 3 = 69.

Sum of **two given numbers** = 11 + 26 = 37.

Third number = Total − Sum of two numbers = 69 − 37 = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average = 23, Number of terms (n) = 3, Number₁ = 11, Number₂ = 26.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all numbers) ÷ (Number of terms)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d329db3c87a79cdfdc43aef2238e422ed2720cb59235d319399783870b6521f.png] 

⇒ Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ Average = (11 + 26 + x) ÷ 3

⇒ 23 = (37 + x) ÷ 3

⇒ 23 × 3 = 37 + x

⇒ 69 = 37 + x

⇒ x = 69 − 37

⇒ x = 32

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

In any set of numbers, the sum of deviations from the average is always zero. Deviation = (Number − Average).

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Average

For numbers in AP, the average is simply the **middle term** (if n is odd) or the average of the **first and last terms**.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: Which statement is correct with reference to Neptunium?

options.text: It was known during Mendeleev’s time.
It is a naturally occurring element found in pitchblende.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It is a naturally occurring element found in pitchblende.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neptunium** is a **naturally occurring element** that is found in trace amounts in ores like **pitchblende**, a uranium-rich mineral.
 
• It is a part of the **actinide series** in the periodic table and has the atomic number **93**.
 
• Neptunium is formed as a byproduct in the decay chain of uranium and thorium, as well as during the operation of nuclear reactors.
 
• It was discovered in **1940** by Edwin McMillan and Philip Abelson at the **University of California, Berkeley.**
 
• The element is **radioactive** and has no stable isotopes. The most common isotope of Neptunium is **Neptunium-237**, which has a half-life of approximately **2.14 million years**.
 
• It is primarily used in **nuclear science** for research purposes and in the production of plutonium-238, which is used in **radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs)** for space missions.
 
• Pitchblende, also known as uraninite, is a principal ore of **uranium** and a source of Neptunium due to its trace presence.
 
• Neptunium is a **silvery metal** with properties similar to uranium and plutonium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** It is non-reactive element**__

 __
 
• Neptunium is a **reactive element**. It reacts with oxygen, acids, and halogens, contrary to the statement that it is non-reactive.
 
• It forms a variety of compounds, including **oxides and halides**, and shows multiple oxidation states ranging from +3 to +7.
 
• Its reactivity is one of the reasons for its use in chemical and nuclear research.
 
 
 
• **It is stable element**__
 __
 
• Neptunium is **radioactive** and does not have any stable isotopes, making the statement incorrect.
 
• Its isotopes decay over time through various processes such as alpha decay, beta decay, and spontaneous fission.
 
 
 
• **It was known during Mendeleev's time**__
 __
 
• Neptunium was not discovered during **Mendeleev's time**. It was only discovered in **1940**, long after Mendeleev developed the periodic table in **1869**.
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table did not include elements beyond uranium (atomic number 92), as transuranic elements like Neptunium were synthesized later.
 
 
 
• **General Information on Pitchblende**__
 
 
• **Pitchblende**, also known as uraninite, is a **black or brownish-black mineral** that is primarily composed of uranium oxide (**UO₂**).
 
• It is an important ore for extracting **uranium** and contains trace amounts of other elements like **radium, thorium, and Neptunium.**
 
• The mineral is found in countries like **Canada, Congo, the Czech Republic, and the United States.**

A retailer offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article.

I. Two successive discounts of 27%.

II. A discount of 36% followed by a discount of 45%.

III. Successive discounts of 19% and 32%.

IV. A discount of 34% followed by a discount of 7%.

Which scheme will fetch the maximum selling price?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To obtain the **maximum selling price**, the **total discount percentage** must be the **minimum**.

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the **net discount** = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Scheme I: 27 + 27 − 7.29 = 46.71% | Scheme II: 36 + 45 − 16.2 = 64.8%.

Scheme III: 19 + 32 − 6.08 = 44.92% | Scheme IV: 34 + 7 − 2.38 = 38.62%.

The **lowest discount** is in **Scheme IV** (38.62%), resulting in the **highest Selling Price**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → Four different **successive discount schemes**. We need to find the one with the **maximum SP**.
Formulas: Net Discount% = a + b − (ab ÷ 100) | SP = MP × (100 − Net Discount%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5b26bb48596f2fcd5ce89786464303a98102b53c1c752e6cf9997739fb0c2f5.png] 
⇒ **Scheme I**: 27 + 27 − (27 × 27 ÷ 100) = 54 − 7.29 = **46.71%**.
⇒ **Scheme II**: 36 + 45 − (36 × 45 ÷ 100) = 81 − 16.2 = **64.8%**.
⇒ **Scheme III**: 19 + 32 − (19 × 32 ÷ 100) = 51 − 6.08 = **44.92%**.
⇒ **Scheme IV**: 34 + 7 − (34 × 7 ÷ 100) = 41 − 2.38 = **38.62%**.
⇒ Since 38.62% is the **minimum discount**, it fetches the **maximum selling price**.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Discount and SP

For a fixed Marked Price (MP), the Selling Price (SP) is inversely proportional to the discount offered. Higher discount means lower SP, and lower discount means higher SP.

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are offered one after another, the net discount is always less than the simple sum of individual discount percentages.</p

questions.question:
If a hemisphere of radius 3 cm is fitted inside a cuboid and then water is filled inside the cuboid, the amount of water (in cm³) present in the cuboid is:

(Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **hemisphere** of radius **r** to be fitted inside a **cuboid**, the smallest cuboid must be a **cube** with side **a = 2r** (for base) and height **h = r**.

Volume of **water** = Volume of **cuboid** − Volume of **hemisphere**.

Volume = (2r × 2r × r) − (2/3 × π × r³) = 4r³ − (2/3 × 3.14 × r³).

Volume = r³ (4 − 2.0933) = 27 × 1.9067 ≈ 51.48 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.48 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Radius of hemisphere (r) = **3 cm**. π = **3.14**.

The **minimum dimensions** of the cuboid to fit the hemisphere are: Length = **6 cm**, Breadth = **6 cm**, and Height = **3 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3e3610c724070b5ca5651166253ba218e347991c317f8aea8afea783463cd61.png] 

⇒ Volume of **Cuboid** = Length × Breadth × Height = 6 × 6 × 3 = **108 cm³**.

⇒ Volume of **Hemisphere** = (2/3) × π × r³ = (2/3) × 3.14 × (3)³.

⇒ Volume of **Hemisphere** = 2 × 3.14 × 9 = **56.52 cm³**.

⇒ Volume of **Water** = 108 − 56.52 = **51.48 cm³**.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.48 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere and Hemisphere

Volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³ and for a hemisphere, it is exactly half: (2/3)πr³.

Fitting Solids in Containers

To fit a sphere of radius **r**, the minimum cube side is **2r**. For a hemisphere, the base requires **2r × 2r** but the height only needs **r**.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr² and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr².</p
